SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=

    SEL_NAMESPACE=""

fi

  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--field-selector "$SEL_FIELDS")
fi

  SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
    '{namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
      label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
      field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

    echo "=== STDERR ==="
    echo "$err_content"
    echo "=== ROWS ==="
    echo "=== COUNT ==="
    echo 0
  fi
  exit 0

    --arg stderr "$err_content" \
    --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
    '{count: $count, header: $header, rows: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

  echo "$header"
  echo "=== ROWS ==="
  echo "$data"
  echo "=== COUNT ==="
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then echo "$data" | wc -l; else echo 0; fi
fi

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=services
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, type: .spec.type, selector: .spec.selector, ports: [.spec.ports[] | {port: .port, targetPort: .targetPort}], clusterIP: .spec.clusterIP}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=events
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items | sort_by(.lastTimestamp) | .[] | {last: .lastTimestamp, type: .type, reason: .reason, obj: (.involvedObject.kind + "/" + .involvedObject.name), count: .count, msg: .message}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash

# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.

# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'

[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, conditions: [.status.conditions[] | {type: .type, status: .status, reason: .reason, msg: .message}], allocatable: .status.allocatable, capacity: .status.capacity, taints: .spec.taints}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).

  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

## 本轮结论

### 已证实（第 1 轮的判断成立）
- **recommendationservice 被缩容到 0 确实是真因之一**。恢复后 frontend 的 `failed to get product recommendations ... dial tcp 10.96.63.235:8080: connect: connection refused` 告警从 19:44:03 持续到 **19:44:36**（新 Pod 19:43:40 创建、启动期间 Service 无可用后端），之后完全消失；Endpoints 里已有 `10.244.0.173:8080`。这也解释 p99 从 422ms → 243ms、>180ms 从 9.0% → 5.6%。
- 12 个 Deployment 均 1/1 Ready、restartCount=0、所有 Service Endpoints 均非空。

### 已被推翻
- **cartservice 的卡顿不是它自己的 CPU 配额造成的**。CPU 上限已从 300m 提到 1，但**新 Pod（19:43:47 创建）在 19:45:29 仍然报** `Readiness probe failed: timeout: failed to connect service "10.244.0.174:7070" within 1s`（gRPC 探针在容器内执行，1s 内连健康检查都拿不到响应）。所以 CPU 上限不是根因。

### 仍然存在、且已定位到具体一跳
未解释的长尾其实全部落在**购物车调用**上（日志覆盖最近 10 分钟，frontend 共 6,404 行，其中 129 条完成日志 took_ms ≥ 100ms；示例：`/` 243/246/247ms、`/product/*` 211–227、若干 424–440ms、`/cart` 201–227、`POST /cart` 199–300、`POST /cart/checkout` 214/239）——**所有页面类型都慢，唯一共同依赖是 cartservice**。

用 currencyservice 的时间戳可以把延迟夹逼出来（product 页顺序是 getProduct → getCurrencies → **getCart** → convert → recommendations → ads）：

| frontend 请求 | GetSupportedCurrencies | Convert 完成 | 间隔 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 27a98575（223ms） | 19:45:46.259（+1ms） | 19:45:46.476 | **217ms 落在 getCart** |
| 1b05dcfa（214ms） | 19:45:48.676 | 19:45:48.884 | **208ms** |
| 4f1d8b65（161ms） | 19:45:49.513 | 19:45:49.665 | **152ms** |
| 2263059d（8ms，正常） | 19:45:46.867 | 19:45:46.869 | 2ms |

且卡顿结束后 recommendations（46.478）和 ads（46.480）都在 2–4ms 内返回 → **不是 ads/currency/recommendation/productcatalog**；同期多个请求会在同一毫秒一起完成（如 19:44:09.814041265 与 …365、19:46:26.0535/0548、19:41:15.0070/0087），是"一个共享阻塞点同时放行所有请求"的特征，延迟呈 ~210ms / ~430ms 量化（≈100ms CFS 周期的 2–4 倍）。

### 仍未确定的部分（如实说明）
卡点位于 **cartservice ↔ redis-cart** 之间：要么 redis-cart 的 **125m CPU 上限**（本命名空间最低，Redis 8 + RedisSearch/TimeSeries 模块后台线程的突发很容易撞上 12.5ms/100ms 配额，正好产生 200–440ms 的量化延迟），要么 cartservice 在 **128Mi 内存上限**下 .NET 的 GC 暂停。没有 metrics 工具集、且 nodes/其他命名空间无权读取，无法直接看 cgroup 的 throttling 或内存用量，因此两者无法百分百区分。

### 本轮申请的操作（针对性 + 零风险排除）
- `set_cpu_limit redis-cart 1`：消除唯一可疑的 CPU 节流点（只提高上限，不降任何东西）。
- `set_cpu_limit frontend 1`：把"frontend 自身被 200m 节流"这条分支也排除掉（延迟点夹在两个 frontend 动作之间，无法只靠日志排除）。

如果这轮之后仍有 ~200ms 长尾，则剩下的解释只有 cartservice 的内存上限（128Mi → 建议 512Mi）或单节点 CPU 争抢——**这两项不在本轮可申请的操作清单里，需要运维直接处理**。

```json
{"root_causes": [{"object": "cartservice / redis-cart", "cause": "购物车调用（cartservice GetCart/AddItem）仍间歇性阻塞 ~200–430ms、偶发 >1s：所有剩余慢请求都落在需要读购物车的路径（/、/product/*、/cart、POST /cart、POST /cart/checkout）；以 currencyservice 日志逐请求夹逼可见 GetSupportedCurrencies 在 +1ms 到达而 Convert 在 +217ms 才发生，延迟全在 getCart。cartservice 自身 gRPC 探针在新 Pod（CPU 上限已提至 1）上仍于 19:45:29 报 1s 超时，故排除其 CPU 配额；卡点在 cartservice↔redis-cart：最可能是 redis-cart 的 125m CPU 上限导致命令被节流（延迟呈 100ms 周期的 2–4 倍量化，且多请求同毫秒一起完成），其次是 cartservice 在 128Mi 内存上限下的 .NET GC 暂停（需 metrics/cgroup 才能区分，当前无权读取）"}, {"object": "recommendationservice", "cause": "第 1 轮已修复：Deployment 曾被缩容到 0 副本，frontend 每次 ListRecommendations 都 connection refused（19:44:36 之后告警消失，p99 422ms→243ms）"}], "actions": [{"op": "set_cpu_limit", "deployment": "redis-cart", "cpu": "1"}, {"op": "set_cpu_limit", "deployment": "frontend", "cpu": "1"}], "explanation": "提高 redis-cart 的 CPU 上限消除购物车路径上唯一可疑的 CPU 节流点，并把 frontend 上限放宽以排除前端自身被 200m 节流的可能；若下轮仍存在 ~200ms 长尾，则需运维提升 cartservice 内存上限(128Mi)或排查单节点 CPU 争抢，这两项不在可申请操作内。"}
```

Important: cartservice readiness probe still failing at 19:45:29 (count 4) even with CPU limit 1 (new pod started 19:43:47). So the cartservice hang is NOT due to CPU limit of cartservice. It's likely a dependency: redis-cart (CPU limit 125m — extremely low for redis!) or a network issue.

Also note the probe failure message format "timeout: failed to connect service ... within 1s" — this is grpc_health_probe? Actually cartservice uses grpc_health_probe with -addr. The message "timeout: failed to connect service \"10.244.0.174:7070\" within 1s: context deadline exceeded" is characteristic of grpc_health_probe. So the gRPC server accepts TCP but the health RPC doesn't complete in 1s → server is blocked/slow, not connection refused. So cartservice's .NET runtime is blocked — probably waiting on redis (sync calls) or thread pool starvation.

Let me check redis-cart logs and cartservice logs. Also check whether redis-cart has 125m limit → redis is CPU-throttled. With .NET StackExchange.Redis, blocking calls could stall the gRPC threadpool? Actually cartservice uses async. But if redis is slow/throttled, the health check (which may ping redis via ICartStore? no, health check is just server health) — cartservice health check in microservices-demo v0.10 is grpc_health_probe which just calls grpc health check, which responds healthy always. Hmm, but if thread pool starved due to sync-over-async calls to redis, health RPC would time out.

Let me look at logs: cartservice logs, redis-cart logs, frontend logs (for slow request paths), and maybe check node resources. Also check for NetworkPolicy / resource limits on other services.

Also check adservice: adservice 300m CPU limit — adservice is Java, and frontend calls it on home page. Java with 300m CPU limit... possible GC/slow. But round-1's 180ms+ tail now 5.6%.

## 本轮结论

### 已证实（第 1 轮的判断成立）
- **recommendationservice 被缩容到 0 确实是真因之一**。恢复后 frontend 的 `failed to get product recommendations ... dial tcp 10.96.63.235:8080: connect: connection refused` 告警从 19:44:03 持续到 **19:44:36**（新 Pod 19:43:40 创建、启动期间 Service 无可用后端），之后完全消失；Endpoints 里已有 `10.244.0.173:8080`。这也解释 p99 从 422ms → 243ms、>180ms 从 9.0% → 5.6%。
- 12 个 Deployment 均 1/1 Ready、restartCount=0、所有 Service Endpoints 均非空。

### 已被推翻
- **cartservice 的卡顿不是它自己的 CPU 配额造成的**。CPU 上限已从 300m 提到 1，但**新 Pod（19:43:47 创建）在 19:45:29 仍然报** `Readiness probe failed: timeout: failed to connect service "10.244.0.174:7070" within 1s`（gRPC 探针在容器内执行，1s 内连健康检查都拿不到响应）。所以 CPU 上限不是根因。

### 仍然存在、且已定位到具体一跳
未解释的长尾其实全部落在**购物车调用**上（日志覆盖最近 10 分钟，frontend 共 6,404 行，其中 129 条完成日志 took_ms ≥ 100ms；示例：`/` 243/246/247ms、`/product/*` 211–227、若干 424–440ms、`/cart` 201–227、`POST /cart` 199–300、`POST /cart/checkout` 214/239）——**所有页面类型都慢，唯一共同依赖是 cartservice**。

用 currencyservice 的时间戳可以把延迟夹逼出来（product 页顺序是 getProduct → getCurrencies → **getCart** → convert → recommendations → ads）：

| frontend 请求 | GetSupportedCurrencies | Convert 完成 | 间隔 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 27a98575（223ms） | 19:45:46.259（+1ms） | 19:45:46.476 | **217ms 落在 getCart** |
| 1b05dcfa（214ms） | 19:45:48.676 | 19:45:48.884 | **208ms** |
| 4f1d8b65（161ms） | 19:45:49.513 | 19:45:49.665 | **152ms** |
| 2263059d（8ms，正常） | 19:45:46.867 | 19:45:46.869 | 2ms |

且卡顿结束后 recommendations（46.478）和 ads（46.480）都在 2–4ms 内返回 → **不是 ads/currency/recommendation/productcatalog**；同期多个请求会在同一毫秒一起完成（如 19:44:09.814041265 与 …365、19:46:26.0535/0548、19:41:15.0070/0087），是"一个共享阻塞点同时放行所有请求"的特征，延迟呈 ~210ms / ~430ms 量化（≈100ms CFS 周期的 2–4 倍）。

### 仍未确定的部分（如实说明）
卡点位于 **cartservice ↔ redis-cart** 之间：要么 redis-cart 的 **125m CPU 上限**（本命名空间最低，Redis 8 + RedisSearch/TimeSeries 模块后台线程的突发很容易撞上 12.5ms/100ms 配额，正好产生 200–440ms 的量化延迟），要么 cartservice 在 **128Mi 内存上限**下 .NET 的 GC 暂停。没有 metrics 工具集、且 nodes/其他命名空间无权读取，无法直接看 cgroup 的 throttling 或内存用量，因此两者无法百分百区分。

### 本轮申请的操作（针对性 + 零风险排除）
- `set_cpu_limit redis-cart 1`：消除唯一可疑的 CPU 节流点（只提高上限，不降任何东西）。
- `set_cpu_limit frontend 1`：把"frontend 自身被 200m 节流"这条分支也排除掉（延迟点夹在两个 frontend 动作之间，无法只靠日志排除）。

如果这轮之后仍有 ~200ms 长尾，则剩下的解释只有 cartservice 的内存上限（128Mi → 建议 512Mi）或单节点 CPU 争抢——**这两项不在本轮可申请的操作清单里，需要运维直接处理**。

```json
{"root_causes": [{"object": "cartservice / redis-cart", "cause": "购物车调用（cartservice GetCart/AddItem）仍间歇性阻塞 ~200–430ms、偶发 >1s：所有剩余慢请求都落在需要读购物车的路径（/、/product/*、/cart、POST /cart、POST /cart/checkout）；以 currencyservice 日志逐请求夹逼可见 GetSupportedCurrencies 在 +1ms 到达而 Convert 在 +217ms 才发生，延迟全在 getCart。cartservice 自身 gRPC 探针在新 Pod（CPU 上限已提至 1）上仍于 19:45:29 报 1s 超时，故排除其 CPU 配额；卡点在 cartservice↔redis-cart：最可能是 redis-cart 的 125m CPU 上限导致命令被节流（延迟呈 100ms 周期的 2–4 倍量化，且多请求同毫秒一起完成），其次是 cartservice 在 128Mi 内存上限下的 .NET GC 暂停（需 metrics/cgroup 才能区分，当前无权读取）"}, {"object": "recommendationservice", "cause": "第 1 轮已修复：Deployment 曾被缩容到 0 副本，frontend 每次 ListRecommendations 都 connection refused（19:44:36 之后告警消失，p99 422ms→243ms）"}], "actions": [{"op": "set_cpu_limit", "deployment": "redis-cart", "cpu": "1"}, {"op": "set_cpu_limit", "deployment": "frontend", "cpu": "1"}], "explanation": "提高 redis-cart 的 CPU 上限消除购物车路径上唯一可疑的 CPU 节流点，并把 frontend 上限放宽以排除前端自身被 200m 节流的可能；若下轮仍存在 ~200ms 长尾，则需运维提升 cartservice 内存上限(128Mi)或排查单节点 CPU 争抢，这两项不在可申请操作内。"}
```

Round 2: 12/215 >180ms (5.6%), p99 243ms, p90 29ms, median 8ms.

But what if the recommendation service — freshly restarted — has an inefficiency, e.g., 220ms to serve ListRecommendations sometimes? We measured recommendations at +220ms after frontend start for slow requests... but the recommendation log line arrives when the RPC arrives at the server; so no.

Hmm, but wait: In my analysis, I assumed getProduct comes before getCurrencies. Let me double check with the actual v0.10.3 source. frontend/handlers.go productHandler:

```go

	log := r.Context().Value(ctxKeyLog{}).(logrus.FieldLogger)
	id := mux.Vars(r)["id"]

```

```go
	recommendations, err := fe.getRecommendations(...)
	if err != nil {
		log.WithField("error", err).Warn("failed to get product recommendations")
	}
	// ignore errors - this call is optional
	fe.chooseAd(r.Context(), p.GetCategories(), log)
```
Yes recommendations then ads. We saw recommendations at .4783 and ads at .4805 — consistent!

And the currency conversion at .476 came right before recommendations. So the sequence: getProduct(?), getCurrencies @46.259, getCart → 217ms, convertCurrency @46.476, recommendations @46.478, ads @46.480, response @46.481.

Yes: getCart is the stall. Solid.

But hmm, wait: this suggests getProduct took ≤1ms, and getCurrencies arrived at +1ms after the whole request started. That means the request-start → 3 gRPC round trips all in 1.3ms. Fast.

OK. Now, decision on actions. Let me consider one more diagnostic angle to decide redis vs cartservice: the *checkout* path. checkoutservice calls cartservice GetCart (its own connection) AND redis? no. We saw POST /cart/checkout slow at 214/239ms — consistent with either.

Another angle: redis memory 200Mi request / 256Mi limit on a node... if redis hit its memory limit, it'd be OOMKilled. Not killed.

Another: the redis liveness probe (tcpSocket, timeout 1s, period 5s) never failed → redis's TCP accept was always responsive. If redis were CPU-throttled for 200ms, the tcpSocket probe (kernel-level accept) would still succeed. So no info.

Conversely, cartservice's gRPC probe failed → the cartservice *container* was unable to serve for >1s. Since grpc_health_probe runs inside the container, this could be container-level CPU starvation OR app-level stall.

If the app were stalled due to a *redis* pause, the health check (no redis) would still respond fast... UNLESS the health check in cartservice v0.10.3 does touch the cart store! Let me consider: cartservice v0.10.3 Startup.cs:

builder.Services.AddGrpcHealthChecks().AddCheck<CartServiceHealthCheck>("cart");
```
Hmm, I'm not sure. In the microservices-demo cartservice, there's `CartServiceHealthCheck`? Actually I recall in cartservice `Program.cs`:

builder.Services.AddGrpcHealthChecks().AddCheck("self", () => HealthCheckResult.Healthy());
```

Option 1: Raise redis-cart CPU limit 125m → 1 (and maybe 500m). If redis is the bottleneck → fixed.
Option 2: Restart cartservice → clears any state; if it's GC/heap pressure, a fresh pod is the same as before (new pod already showed stalls) → no.
